newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rubber exports seen falling sharply.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rubber exports seen falling sharply.

text.p: Rising demand for rubber from Sri Lanka's manufacturing industry is expected to cut Sri Lanka's raw rubber exports sharply by 2000, a top rubber industry official said on Friday.
"The rubber-based industry has grown phenomenally over the last five years," William Tissa Ellawala, chairman of the Colombo Rubber Traders Association, said in an interview.
"By the year 2000 we estimate that as much as 50 percent of all rubber made in Sri Lanka will be used locally in value-added rubber based products," he said.
Raw rubber exports, Sri Lanka's biggest export commodity after tea, fell to 68.2 million kg in 1995 from the previous year's 69.1 million, the government's Rubber Development Department said.
Sri Lanka's 1995 rubber production of 105.7 million kg was up only marginally from the previous year's 105.3 million kg.
Domestic consumption was growing with new glove, tyre and other rubber-based industries being set up, said Ellawala whose association groups rubber growers, exporters and brokers.
"The rubber-based industry in this country is only a very recent development," he said.

Ellawala said that 10 years ago only 15 percent of domestically produced rubber was used in the local rubber industry. "By 1992 we used 28 percent in local rubber-based industry and last year the figure was 38 percent -- a very sharp increase," he added.
Exporters said production this year was expected to be around the same as 1995 because rain has affected tapping.
The country produces only two percent of the world's rubber and is now ranked the eighth-biggest producer in the world, down from the fourth-biggest in 1980.
